outcome.technical: Fetched the six windows cells of run 40715565769 with gh run view --job <id> --log (all exit 0) into scratchpad/costs1444/{plain1,plain2,plain3,cp1,cp2,cp3}.log. WHICH LEG: ci.yml:139-143's recipe says to save each windows cell's log, concatenate them and record with --platform windows-latest. costs_from_render's docstring (tools/sweep-selftests.py) says a file printed more than once keeps its LONGEST timing, because the slower run is the one the timeouts must fit, and that a FAILED line counts as a floor. So I recorded from ALL SIX cells, plain and cp1252, concatenated (windows-all.log), and not from the plain legs alone as the brief's description says. The brief's --platform win32 also differs from ci.yml's windows-latest, which the existing table already carried, so I kept windows-latest and passed --workers 4 to match the table's existing workers field. Command: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log windows-all.log --platform windows-latest --workers 4 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json. It printed 'recorded 193 files' seconds' and exited 0. FAILED SHARDS: plain1/cp1 (test_drive_phase.py) and plain3/cp3 (test_audit_status.py, tools/prove-gates.py) still print usable per-file rows. One read covers every swept file: the log has 193 rows against 193 swept files, so no file keeps its old figure. The 16 files the old table lacked now have entries, and none were dropped. The figures from failed runs are taken as floors, as the tool's own docstring says. cp1's test_drive_phase figure of 4913.5 includes ar-block killed at 447s, so the true cost is at least that. plain1's 4375.4 had no block killed (no DID NOT REPORT in plain1.log), though ar20-ar22 failed on cases that P144.3 has since fixed. The test_audit_status and prove-gates failures were case failures of about 30s, not timeouts. BEFORE/AFTER test_drive_phase.py: 1346.4 -> 4913.5 slot-seconds (the plain legs alone would give 4375.4). Calibrated ar-block timeout (file_timeout at stage_grant(4)=3 slots): 1347s -> 4914s (4376s on plain alone). Both exceed SWEEP_DEADLINE 1380, so on CI every drive_phase block is now cut to the deadline's remainder. INFERENCE from file_timeout's cap: the 447s that killed ar-block in cp1 was already that remainder, not the 1347s calibration, so re-recording does not change what killed it. CONSEQUENCE, AND WHY THIS IS NOT GREEN: case tt5 in tools/sweep-selftests.py asserts that no calibrated timeout on the live table exceeds SWEEP_DEADLINE. On the new table it FAILS: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --selftest exit 1, 'SELFTEST FAILED: 143/144 cases passed', with FAIL tt5 '... deadline 1380s + setup 120s vs 26 minutes; longest file timeout 4914s'. The same command on a clone of HEAD 3bcd5772 with the old table exits 0, ALL PASS 144/144, 'longest file timeout 1347s'. So the selftests gate goes red because of this change, through a file outside this task's scope. The plain-only table fails tt5 too (4376s), so the choice of legs does not decide it. The fix needs a decision in tools/sweep-selftests.py, perhaps ci.yml too: the block-timeout derivation from whole-file cost (true per-block costs, P142-R9 / P143.6, which this task does not settle), or tt5's invariant together with SWEEP_DEADLINE and the selftests job's timeout-minutes. I did not cap or edit any figure to make tt5 pass. SPLIT (--shard I/3, CI matrix N=3): there is no --list flag, so I computed it with the tool's own shard_paths() in scratchpad/costs1444/probe.py. Before: 60/66/67 files at 1681.5/1681.5/1681.4 slot-s. After: 1/97/95 files at 4913.5/2893.1/2893.1. test_drive_phase.py now sits alone in shard 1 and the other two shards are equal. That is as balanced as greedy can make it, since sh3's bound is the single costliest file. But shard 1's wall floor is 4913.5/4 slots = about 1228s against a 1380s deadline, about 150s of slack, so the drive_phase shard stays the critical path. TIMEOUT_PER_COST check, which its comment asks for at each re-record: in this run's plain and cp1252 legs, among files that took 20s or more on a leg, the widest spread is 1.83x (test__tree_stamp.py 21.8/11.9), then 1.68x (test_stamp_verification.py). Both are above the 1.51x the comment records, so that comment is now stale; a factor of 3 still covers the spread. Measured over one run, two legs. DEPENDANTS: ci.yml - its recipe (139-143) is the one followed and is still correct. Its selftests timeout-minutes of 26 is what tt5 compares against, and tt5 fails on it now: needs a decision, no edit made. stamp-verification.py - still correct: sized_deadline reads the table's figure times TIMEOUT_PER_COST, capped at MAX_TIMEOUT, so a red-first run naming test_drive_phase.py gets a longer deadline, up to the cap. tests/test_stamp_verification.py - still correct: _sweep_repo commits its own fixture costs and never reads the live table. tools/sweep-selftests.py - CHANGED IN EFFECT: tt5 is red, and the comment above SWEEP_DEADLINE (~lines 225-229) naming test_drive_phase.py at 1347s and the 1.51x spread in the TIMEOUT_PER_COST comment are now stale. No edit: out of scope. CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md (314-330), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (4897) - still correct: they describe the table and --record-costs without quoting any figure from it. Logs, candidate tables (cand-all.json, cand-plain.json, before.json) and selftest logs are in scratchpad/costs1444/. claims: 1 n/a - no behaviour-claiming prose written; the table's 'about' text is record_costs()'s own (sweep-selftests.py record_costs) | 2 n/a - no check touched; tt5 observed red on the new table and green on HEAD's, both runs shown above | 3 n/a - not a fix of a reported defect | 4 n/a - no rule to an agent | 5 spread measured over one run's two windows legs (plain and cp1252 cells of 40715565769), 1.83x widest; no second run, so stated as measured once | 6 n/a - no guard | 7 every figure here carries its command: table entries come from --costs-from-log, timeouts from file_timeout/tt5's printout, the split from shard_paths in probe.py
outcome.descriptive: The windows cost table is re-recorded from all six windows cells: test_drive_phase.py goes from 1346.4 to 4913.5 slot-seconds and gets a shard to itself, but its calibrated block timeout (4914s) now exceeds the 1380s CI deadline, so sweep-selftests' tt5 is red and the task cannot be green without an out-of-scope change to tools/sweep-selftests.py (and maybe ci.yml)
